text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Prime Minister Hariri and supporters win 14 seats in the parliamentary elections; he calls for a dialogue with the opposition.
-Ex-premier Hoss, who won re-election, dismisses the latest polls as a sham.
-Lebanon's balance of payments posts a surplus of $180 million in the first seven months of 1996.
-Syrian Foreign Minister Shara says Syria will not sign peace with Israel without Lebanon.
-Israeli jets stage mock raids over some parts of south Lebanon.
-Fears of an electoral battle in south Lebanon rise in light of the failure of Amal and Hizbollah to reach a coalition.
-Radical Christian MP Wakim says he will sue Hariri and Interior Minister Murr for carrying out fraud in the elections.
-Hizbollah will announce its list for the south Lebanon elections on Friday.
-Lebanon's trade balance improves by 3.5 percent in January-July.
-Hizbollah says PM Hariri is a danger and incites sectarianism in Lebanon.
